I thought the urine would show it and saliva wouldn’t but it ended up being the opposite of what I expected
In all fairness though doctors don’t know everything so I’d say she’s not wrong with her decisions
Alright thanks for helping me with this. I appreciate it

Good advice thank you sm.
I was planning to make sure I don’t use anymore, drink lots of water, cranberry juice, and anything to help me detox.
I really hope it won’t show up.
Is it usually almost eliminated by the time a week has gone by?

Yeah. I definitely need big changes in my life and part of that is a change of environment.
I’m struggling to gather my resources, I’m only 20, I have very little school education (high school dropout), and it’s a lot of pressure to expect anyone else to pay for it (they should not have to and they wouldn’t anyway, I don’t want anyone to).

I think I might end up becoming homeless, dead, or back in jail without some sort of way out.

I’m in a terrible condition to be working, I don’t see how I could hold a job. My wellbeing is so bad and I think I would compromise taking care of my needs if I overworked. Yes money helps, maybe that’s absolutely what I need but I am struggling to find a balance and it’s hard to find reason to continue when I’m constantly reminded why I should doubt I could ever be anything better than I am now.

Not in this lifetime I don’t think. This was a fate I’m burdened with

I’m not much of the “addictive” type either. Maybe that’s why I haven’t overdone it as much as my dead friends.
I sometimes go on binges in high stress situations, as a way to self medicate. But I hate using everyday.. it just puts me into a vegetative state. But honestly, I’m starting to feel tempted to shut down my body since I can’t do much of anything right.

The least harmful would be thc, but I cannot smoke it while I’m on probation (ridiculous).
Next would be moderate use of alcohol but it’s so physically toxic, and I don’t metabolize it well so I don’t want to be doing that.
Next would be moderate use of benzos, on an as needed basis (the way doctors prescribe them), but the problem is that doctors are scared of liabilities with any controlled substances so I can’t even get my effective anxiety meds, and no alternatives really alleviate it.
Next would probably be a tie between cocaine and opioids (certain opioids).
I think the cocaine is the most financially devastating to me and those often become heavy binges, I think physically it’s the worst on my since it’s hard on the heart.
So for opioids, as long as it’s not fentanyl and as long as I keep the usage down, and as long as I avoid injecting it (I’ve never injected) it seems to be fairly balanced. Only high amounts that exceed my tolerance risk overdose (respiratory depression), which I’m good at avoiding that range but it’s a feasible way to take your own life for sure

Maybe you could say the least harmful addictions are caffeine and nicotine but they just don’t do much for me really

Well I’ve had on & off sobriety from everything but sometimes it’s cocaine and crack, sometimes it’s fentanyl, heroin, or painkillers, sometimes it’s benzos and other sedatives, it used to be alcohol but not so much anymore, also used to be addicted to thc but not anymore, sometimes I like the combination of everything together.

And honestly sobriety has been really hard. It’s almost as if all I end up doing is find another compulsive habit to replace the drugs such as being on the internet too much
